Getting started

Everyone

PlanPlate runs in the web browser on a computer, tablet or phone. There is nothing to install.

Sign in or create an account

  1. Open PlanPlate and use the sign-in box on the home page.
  2. New here? Choose Create account, enter your name, email and a password, and accept the terms.
  3. Were you invited by your restaurant? Sign up with the same email address the invitation went to. The restaurant is already waiting in your list.

Your restaurants

After signing in you land on Restaurants. Each card shows today's hours, bookings, guests and seats, plus a badge with your role (Owner, Manager or Staff). A yellow banner lists bookings waiting for approval, and the bell at the top shows the same count on every page.

  • Open goes to the restaurant's Today page.
  • Bookings goes straight to Reservations.
  • New restaurant adds another restaurant to your account.

Who can do what

Owners and managers

Everyone signs in with their own email. What they see depends on their role at each restaurant.

OwnerManagerStaff (waiters, hosts)
Today, Reservations, walk-ins, seatingYesYesYes
Approve or decline requestsYesYesYes
Guest bookYesYesLook up only
Hours, tables, events, menu, gallery, website, website elements, QR codesYesYesNo
Settings (booking rules, approvals, emails)YesYesNo
Invite people and change their roleYesYesNo
Delete the restaurantYesNoNo

A manager sees every tab:

A waiter (Staff) sees only the three tabs they need to run the room:

Nobody can change or remove their own access. That way no one locks themselves out by mistake.

Give someone access by email

Owners and managers

Owners and managers can give someone access with just their email address.

  1. Open the restaurant and go to Settings, then Team (the last item in the list on the left).
  2. Type the person's email address.
  3. Pick Staff for a waiter or host, or Manager for someone who should also change settings.
  4. Press Invite.

PlanPlate emails them an invitation. When they sign in, or create an account, with that same email, the restaurant appears in their list. Until then they show as invited.

Change or remove access

Each person on the team has a role menu and a remove button. Change Staff to Manager (or back) and it applies the next time their page loads. Remove someone who has left and they lose access right away. The owner's row can't be changed, and neither can your own.

Today

Everyone

Today is the restaurant's front page: whether you are open right now, and what the day looks like.

  • Open now / Closed, with today's hours. Managers can press Change today's hours or Close today for a one-off change, such as a burst pipe or a private party.
  • Four numbers: bookings today, guests today, guests in the room now, and requests waiting for approval. Tap one to open Reservations.
  • Who's coming: the next arrivals. Tap Seat when a party arrives and Finish when they leave.
  • Photo of the day: press Post to share today's dish or the terrace in the sun. It shows at the top of your website for 3 days.
  • Specials, Coming up (events) and The week ahead fill the rest of the page.

Reservations: the host stand

Everyone

Reservations is the page to keep open on the host-stand tablet. It checks for new bookings every minute and keeps the screen awake; Refresh loads the latest at once, and the time beside it says when the page last updated. With Chime on it plays a short sound when a booking or request arrives. Tap the page once first, because browsers only play sound after a tap.

Requests waiting for approval

Bookings that need a decision appear at the top: for example, the restaurant was nearly full at that time, the party is large, or tables have to be pushed together. Each card says why it is waiting and how full you would be if you accept. When tables must be pushed together (or another party moved first), the card says exactly what to do, and Approve does the move for you.

  • Approve confirms the booking and emails the guest.
  • Decline turns it down and emails the guest.
  • Details opens the full booking, and See the day shows that date.

Three views of the day

Use Previous day, Next day and Today to move between dates, then switch views:

  • Timeline: one row per table across the day, with a red line for now. Click an empty spot on a table's row to book it at that time. Striped bookings are waiting for approval, and a star marks a regular.
  • List: every booking of the day in time order. Each row has a one-tap next step: Approve a request, Seat a guest who has arrived, Finish a table that has left. Tap the row itself to open the booking.
  • Upcoming: every booking still to come, from today onwards.
Day sheet prints the day's bookings for the kitchen or the pass.

Add a booking or a walk-in

Everyone

A booking by phone or in person

  1. On Reservations, press New booking. The form opens at once; a moment later the line under Table shows the best free table.
  2. Pick the date and the number of guests. Times that day shows every time: tap a free one to use it (“+” means tables get pushed together; greyed out means no room). Stays for is how long the table is held. Dates and times that have already passed can't be booked.
  3. Leave Table on Best free table, or pick one. The line under it shows the best fit and how full you'll be. If no single table fits, it says which tables PlanPlate will push together (and which party it moves to make room).
  4. Add the guest's name, phone and email. Taken by records how the booking came in.
  5. Guest's requests is what the guest asked for. Staff note is for the team only: guests never see it.
  6. Leave Email the guest a confirmation ticked to send one (when there's an email address), then save.

If the time is full, PlanPlate says so and offers Save anyway for when you know you can squeeze them in.

A walk-in

Press Walk-in and tap the number of people. They are seated now, at the best free table. To add a name or a note, press Add a name or a note instead.

Change, cancel or mark a no-show

Tap any booking to open it. From there you can change the details or press Approve, Decline, Seat now, Finished, No-show or Cancel booking. Call and Email links reach the guest, and Guest link opens the page the guest sees. A booking cancelled by mistake can be brought back with Restore booking.

The guest book

Everyone

Guests is your guest book. Everyone who has booked is in it automatically, with their visits, how many people they brought, no-shows and cancellations. Search by name, phone, email or tag, and sort with the menu on the right.

Tap a guest to open their card:

  • Tags such as Regular, VIP, Allergy or Birthday. Tags show as badges on their bookings, so the whole team sees them.
  • Team notes: "likes the corner table", "allergic to shellfish". The guest never sees these.
  • Visits and bookings: every past and future booking.
Staff can look guests up. Only owners and managers can change tags and notes.

Opening hours and special days

Managers

Guests can only book when you are open, so get your hours right first.

Regular hours and periods

A period sets the hours for each weekday between two dates, or for the whole year. You can have more than one: when periods overlap, the shorter one wins. So a "Summer" period overrides "Regular hours" for those dates. Press Edit on a period to change it, or Add a period for a new one. Two openings in one day (lunch and dinner) are fine.

The calendar on the right shows the hours that apply on each day, month by month.

Special days

Closed for a holiday, or open late for New Year's Eve? Press Add a special day, pick the date (and an end date for several days), give it a label, then choose Closed or Special hours. Special days override every period.

Tables and the floor plan

Managers

Tables & layout is a drawing of your room. PlanPlate uses it to give each booking the best free table, and to push tables together for big parties.

  • Drag tables to where they stand in the room. Tables that really stand next to each other should be next to each other on the plan.
  • Click a table to change its name, seats, shape and area, or untick Available for bookings to take it out of use.
  • Joinable: tick it for light tables staff can move and push together. Untick it for booths, bar seats and tables fixed to the floor; they show a small lock on the plan and are never moved.
  • Add a table puts a new one on the plan.

Big parties

When no single table fits a party, PlanPlate looks for joinable tables side by side (same area, close on the plan) that are free for the whole visit and pushes them together. If another party sits where the join is needed, it suggests moving them to another free table. Online, such a booking always waits for your approval: the request says exactly what to do ("Move Smith (2 at 19:00) from T4 to T7, then push T3 + T4 together"), and approving it does the move for you. Staff bookings made in the booking editor apply it straight away. If nothing fits, the time shows as full and you can take the party by phone.

Try a big party shows what PlanPlate would do for a party size, day and time, with the bookings already made, and lights up the tables on the plan.

Always join some tables is only for tables you keep pushed together at set hours (or a large table you split at quiet times). Choose the hours and days the join applies. Use Layout on (the weekday) and At (the hour) to see the room as guests can book it at that moment.

Events

Managers

Use Events for private parties, wine dinners or live music.

  1. Press Plan an event and fill in the date, the times and a description.
  2. Tick Show it on our website for a public event. For a private party, tick Close online booking during the event; staff can still add bookings by hand.
  3. Press Set up the room to arrange tables just for that event: start from the everyday layout, move tables, and Make one table from several. Save the room when done, and Print gives you the plan for the team.

Menu and specials

Managers

Menu holds your dishes in sections (Entrées, Plats, Desserts...) with prices and dietary labels such as V (vegetarian) and GF (gluten-free). The guest menu that the table QR code opens, your website and the menu widget all update the moment you save.

  • Add a section, then add dishes to it. Use the pencil to edit a dish and the arrows to change the order.
  • When a dish runs out, press Sold out. Press it again when it's back.
  • See the guest menu shows the menu exactly as guests see it.
  • Have a PDF or a photo of your menu? Use Upload a PDF or photo further down the page.
Dishes of the day go in Specials on the Today page. They appear on your website when you add them and disappear when they end.

Gallery

Managers

Gallery holds your photos and decides how they look on your website.

  • Photos in the gallery show in the order you set: drag a photo by the grip in its corner, or use the arrows. The first ones are what guests see first. Use the eye button to show or hide a photo, and add a caption (it helps Google and screen readers).
  • Other photos and videos are kept for specials, events and the website, but don't appear in the gallery.

How it looks

Pick a layout: Mosaic (rows that show every photo whole), Masonry, Spotlight (one big photo and a strip), Slideshow (cinematic, with a slow zoom), Carousel (guests swipe), Editorial (a magazine spread), Grid or Polaroids. Each layout starts with the settings that suit it; then fine-tune the background, photo size, spacing, corners, frame, captions, hover and scroll effects, how many photos show before "See all", and whether a tap opens the photo full screen.

The live preview shows the real gallery, on a computer or a phone. Every change shows on your PlanPlate website and on every site with the gallery code at once. The code itself is on the Elements tab.

Your restaurant's website

Managers

PlanPlate can build a full website for your restaurant from what it already knows: your name, address, hours, menu, photos, specials and events. They stay up to date by themselves.

  1. Open Website and press Start from my details. It takes about 10 minutes. To see a finished one first, press See an example first.
  2. Work through the steps on the left: Web address & colours, then the texts and pictures. The preview on the right shows the site on a Computer or a Phone.
  3. Drag a section by the grip on its left (or use the arrow keys on the grip) to change where it sits on the page; the site's menu follows the same order.
  4. Press Save, then Publish to put it live. Open shows the live site, Download gives you a copy of the files, and Unpublish takes it down.

Website elements: the Reserve button, menu, hours, gallery

Managers

Elements holds every piece of PlanPlate you can paste into your own website, grouped by what it does: Booking, Menu, Opening hours, Photos and For developers. In WordPress paste it into a "Custom HTML" block, in Wix into "Embed code", in Squarespace into a "Code" block. Each one always shows what is in PlanPlate right now, so you paste it once.

The Reserve button

PlanPlate's own Reserve a table button, styled like a "Sign in with Google" button so it always looks professional. Pick a Style (Dark, Brass, Light or Outline), a Shape and a Size, and see it on a light or a dark site in the preview. Tap the preview: it opens your real booking form. Then Copy the code and paste it once, where the button should appear.

  • Booking form inside a page puts the whole form on a "Reservations" page, with nothing to click first.
  • Use your own button instead (under "advanced") is only for a site that already has its own button. Paste it instead of the Reserve button, not as well.

Menu, hours and photos

  • Live menu shows your uploaded menu files (PDFs and photos) as buttons, then the dishes you typed in. Sold-out dishes hide themselves.
  • Live opening hours follow your periods and special days.
  • Photo gallery shows your gallery in the look you chose on the Gallery page. Change the look there and every site with the code follows.

Share links and QR codes

Managers

Share & QR has the QR codes and the plain links to send guests to PlanPlate.

  • QR codes for booking a table, the menu and your website. Use Download PNG for table cards, the window, the door and flyers. The codes open your live pages, so you never need to reprint them when the menu or hours change. There is also a ready-to-print A4 sheet of four table cards.
  • Links to share are for your social pages, your Google Business Profile, messages and email signatures.

The codes you paste into a website (the Reserve button, the menu, opening hours, the gallery) are on the Elements tab.

Settings: booking rules, approvals, emails

Managers

Settings is one long page. Use the list on the left to jump to a part, and press Save changes in the bar at the bottom when you are done (Discard undoes your changes).

  • Details: the name, description, address and contact details guests see.
  • Booking rules: Table time (how long a booking holds its table), Time slots, Last booking before closing, Minimum notice, the Booking window (how many days ahead) and the Largest party online. You can also pause online booking here; guests are then asked to call.
  • Approvals: when a booking confirms itself and when it waits for you (below).
  • Booking form: a note shown on the form, such as "We hold tables for 15 minutes", in each language.
  • Emails: whether guests get emails, the address that receives approval alerts, and the wording of the confirmed, waiting and declined messages.
  • Languages: which languages the booking form offers (English, Français, Latviešu).
  • Team: who has access (see "Give someone access by email").

Approvals

Bookings confirm straight away while there is room. Past these limits a manager decides:

  • Auto-confirm until: once this share of seats is taken at a time, new bookings wait for approval. 100% confirms everything that fits, and 0% sends every booking to you.
  • Large parties: parties bigger than this always wait.
  • When the limit is reached: take requests for you to approve, or stop online booking for that time and invite guests to walk in.
  • Read requests first: tick Wait for me to approve every booking where the guest wrote a request (an allergy, a high chair, a birthday).

The waiter's view (Staff)

Staff

This part is for waiters and hosts. Your manager adds you by email (see "Give someone access by email"). You then sign in, or create an account, with that email.

The restaurant appears on your Restaurants page with a Staff badge. Press Open (Today) or Bookings (Reservations).

You have three tabs:

  • Today: who's coming next, with Seat and Finish.
  • Reservations: approve or decline requests, take phone bookings and walk-ins, seat guests, finish tables, and mark no-shows.
  • Guests: look up a guest's visits, tags and the team's notes before they arrive.

A typical service

  1. Open Reservations on the host-stand tablet and leave it open. It updates by itself, keeps the screen awake, and chimes for new bookings.
  2. When a party arrives, tap Seat on their row.
  3. Walk-ins: Walk-in, then tap the number of people.
  4. When a table leaves, tap Finish, so the table shows free again.
  5. Someone didn't come? Open their booking and press No-show. The guest book remembers it.

Opening hours, tables, the menu and settings are for managers. Ask a manager if something there needs changing.

On a phone or tablet

Staff

Everything works on a phone or tablet too. The pages stack into one column, the tabs scroll sideways, and the buttons are big enough to tap during service. Restaurants and You (your profile) sit at the bottom of the screen.

On a tablet at the host stand, add PlanPlate to the home screen (in the browser's share or menu button, Add to Home Screen) so it is one tap away.

What your guests see

Everyone

It helps to know what your guests see, so you can answer their questions.

The booking form

Guests reach it from your website, the Book a table QR code or the link on the Share page. They pick the number of guests, a day and a free time, then enter their name, email and phone (the fields marked with a star are required). The form offers only times when you are open and have a table free, including big parties that fit when tables are pushed together (those wait for your approval). They can switch language at the top.

There is one optional box: PlanPlate news and offers, which may include discounts on future bookings (never on the booking being made). EU law doesn't allow it to be ticked in advance. Above the Book button a short line tells guests that by booking they accept your privacy notice and PlanPlate's, with links to both.

After booking, the guest gets an email and a private link to their booking. There they can change or cancel it, and switch off PlanPlate news. If their booking needs your approval, they see that it is waiting, and they get an email when you approve or decline it.

The guest menu

The The menu QR code opens your live menu, with prices, dietary labels and today's specials. Sold-out dishes disappear as soon as you mark them.

Your profile

Everyone

Tap the circle with your initials (top right, or You on a phone) to open your profile.

  • Your name: shown to the rest of the team.
  • Appearance: follow your device, or always Light or Dark (dark is easier on the eyes in a dim dining room).
  • Password: Email me a reset link to choose a new one.
  • Submit feedback: tell us about a problem or an idea.
  • Sign out: always sign out on a shared device.
The person who pays for PlanPlate also sees the plan here, with Manage billing for invoices and the card on file.
PlanPlate · questions or ideas: use Submit feedback at the bottom of any PlanPlate page.
